rv.q: Felicity Kendal steals the show in this delightfully frothy musical
Nothing can obscure Porter's smart lyrics and the production's upbeat, feel-good nature.
It's the women who impress in this reworked, airy Cole Porter musical set among a glamorous but feckless American elite.
Immaculate in its song and dance, it is smoothly staged...
This revival of Cole Porter's beloved musical comedy is a triumphant reminder that golden age musicals, when staged with this much flair and heart, remain impossible to resist.
In some ways, it is difficult to care too much about what is going on, especially if, like me, you’re not inclined to pay much (if any) attention to celebrity gossip.
But it's an enjoyable watch nonetheless, and a worthy addition to the dependably crowdpleasing Barbican Cole Porter canon.
High Society is an evening of pure theatrical pleasure.
Kavanaugh has created exactly the sort of glamorous, big-hearted musical audiences are craving now.
One of the most entertaining musicals you will see this summer, High Society will easily make you fall in love.

cn.t: Cole Porter's score shines in this smoothly staged but somewhat hollow production, with strong performances from the women—particularly Felicity Kendal and Helen George—delivering feel-good froth that doesn't quite reach the heights of previous Barbican revivals.
